index.page:
This project asks whether we can learn a better kernel, potentially input-dependent, other than exp.

Concretely, an attention output is given by
$$
o_t=\sum_{s\le t}p(z_{ts})\,v_s
$$
where $z_{ts} \sim q_t^\top k_s$ is the attention score. In a standard transformer, we have $p=\text{softmax}$.

Our goal is to learn a function $p$ based on the data, which can potentially depend on the activation that goes into the attention layer. We will primarily focus on polynomials, but also test out different function classes.
index.reference: Every run follows this recipe unless its page says otherwise.

runs-2p5x-chinchilla.polynomials: $W$ decay applies weight decay to the coefficient generator's projection $W$; fixed Taylor and static have no $W$.

runs-4k-sequences.sequences: Each model trained on 2,048-token and on 4,096-token sequences with the same budget of 4B tokens: 128 sequences per update at 4k instead of 256.

runs-dense.page:
> [!info] Dense model
> $$c_r(x_t) = \frac{1}{r!}\left[b_r + \frac{1}{\sqrt{K}} \sum_{j=1}^{K} V_{rj} \tanh(w_j^\top x_t)\right]$$
>
> We also test a sigmoid variant:
>
> $$c_r(x_t) = \frac{1}{r!\sqrt{K}} \sum_{j=1}^{K} V_{rj}\, \sigma(w_j^\top x_t)$$

runs-fox-alibi.comparison: Every polynomial is the query-dependent $p_t$ at $m = 4$, except the static row's learned static coefficients. PaTH and FoX–PaTH use PaTH in place of RoPE.
runs-fox-alibi.page:
> [!info] Models
> Suppressing layer and head indices, let $x_t$ be the pre-attention RMSNorm activation and $s_{t,i} = q_t^\top k_i/\sqrt{d_K}$ the score of key $i \le t$. The query-dependent polynomial is
> $$p_t(s) = \sum_{r=0}^{4} \frac{b_r + a_r \tanh(W_r^\top x_t)}{r!}\, s^r.$$
> Each gate decays a key's weight with its distance,
> $$\omega_{t,i} = p_t(s_{t,i})\, e^{-\gamma G_{t,i}}, \qquad \gamma = e^{A_{\log}} > 0,$$
> and the output is $o_t = \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{\mathrm{head}}\big(\sum_{i \le t} \omega_{t,i} v_i\big)$.
>
> | Gate | $G_{t,i}$ |
> |---|---|
> | FoX | $\sum_{j=i+1}^{t} \mathrm{softplus}(w_q^\top x_j + \beta)$ |
> | Query gate | $(t-i)\, \mathrm{softplus}(w_q^\top x_t + \beta)$ |
> | Query gate, sigmoid | $(t-i)\, \sigma(w_q^\top x_t + \beta)$ |
> | Query–key gate | $(t-i)\, \mathrm{softplus}(w_q^\top x_t + w_k^\top x_i + \beta)$ |
> | ALiBi | $t-i$ |
>
> - FoX multiplies GDN-style per-token gates $\alpha_j = e^{-\gamma\, \mathrm{softplus}(w_q^\top x_j + \beta)}$ along the sequence; the other gates apply one rate, from the query or the query–key pair, across the whole distance. With $A_{\log} = 0$, $\alpha_j = \sigma(-w_q^\top x_j - \beta)$: the original FoX sigmoid gate, up to the sign of $w_q$ and $\beta$.
> - ALiBi learns its rate $\gamma = e^{A}$ per layer and head, from ALiBi's slopes and without weight decay; it reads no token. The original ALiBi keeps the slopes fixed.
> - The query–key gate reads the key; the polynomial coefficients read the query only.
> - Per degree: each degree $r$ has its own gate, $\omega_{t,i} = \sum_r c_{t,r}\, s_{t,i}^r\, e^{-\gamma_r G^{(r)}_{t,i}}$.
runs-fox-alibi.query-gates: The polynomials use query + $W$ decay coefficients, which read the query only; exp and softmax use the gate of their row.
runs-fox-alibi.reference: None of these runs use RoPE. The ALiBi runs use fixed slopes (not learned), unlike the polynomial ALiBi above.

runs-other.gates: Query + W decay, where a gate computed from each token scales every degree's coefficient: a sigmoid, or GDN-style at degree 4.
runs-other.input-norm-notes: ![tanh saturation of the coefficient generator by direction, layer 8, head 1, without L2, with L2 after RMSNorm, and with L2 on the raw input](figures/other-runs/saturation-layer8-head1.png)
runs-other.input-norm: The coefficient generator's input scaled to unit L2 norm, after the block's RMSNorm or on the raw input before it; the last variant multiplies a softplus-input SoS polynomial by its input, which adds one to the total degree.
runs-other.learning-rate: Degree-4 query coefficients with the learning rate of $a$ and $b$ tripled; $W$ and the backbone keep theirs, and neither run decays $W$.
runs-other.powers: Polynomials restricted to the even powers 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 or to the constant and the odd powers 1, 3, 5, 7, beside full polynomials of degree 4 and 8.
runs-other.release: Degree-8 query + W decay or static coefficients, held at Taylor for the first 455 updates while the backbone trains, then released all at once or one degree at a time.
runs-other.weight-decay: Degree-4 query and query-key coefficients with weight decay 0.1 on the tanh projection $W$ (both query and key $W$ for query-key), or on $a$, $b$ and $W$; backbone decay is unchanged. The query-key runs also differ in kernel: fused without $W$ decay, Mosaic with it.
runs-other.zero-constant: Degree-8 polynomials, of the softplus of the score or of the raw score, with the constant coefficient fixed at $c_0 = 0$; query variants use W decay.

runs-polynomial.baselines: Our reference model will be exp + head RMSNorm, since it's the best performing.
runs-polynomial.page:
> [!info] Models
> All models compute 
> $$
>     o_t=\operatorname{RMSNorm}\left(\sum_{s\le t}p(z_{ts})\,v_s\right)
> $$
and differ in $p$:
>
> - Exp: $p(z)=e^{z}$
> - Taylor: $p(z)=\sum_{r=0}^{m}z^r/r!$, exp's Taylor series to degree $m$
> - Hermite: $p(z)=e^{1/2}\sum_{r=0}^{m}\mathrm{He}_r(z)/r!$, exp's Hermite series to degree $m$
> - Static: $p(z)=\sum_{r=0}^{m}c_r z^r$, with $c_r$ learned per head
> - Query: $p(z)=\sum_{r=0}^{m}c_r(x_t)\,z^r$, with $c_r(x_t)=b_r+a_r\tanh(w_r^\top x_t)$ and $x_t$ the attention layer's input
> 
> Unless otherwise stated, all applicable models use weight decay on $w_r$.
runs-polynomial.query-key: The $W$-decay run used the Mosaic kernel; the others used the fused kernel.

runs-sos.page:
> [!note] SoS model
>
> Let $s$ be the attention score. The SoS model is given by
> $$h(s;x) = q_1^2(s;x)+q_2^2(s;x)$$
> where $\text{deg}(q_1)=m/2$ and $\text{deg}(q_2)=m/2-1$.

Let $z=\text{softplus}(s)$. We consider three models:

| Variant | Attention weight | Note |
|---|---|---|
| SoS | $h(s)$ | |
| SoS + softplus | $h(z)$ | |
| SoS + softplus prefactor | $z h(z)$ | Raises degree by 1 |

Intuition:
- Softplus: negative scores are first transformed into a small number *and then* fed into $h$. E.g., without it, $x^2$ would treat $-100$ and $100$ equally.
- Softplus prefactor: we additionally get the property that $\text{weight}\to0$ as $s\to-\infty$.
runs-sos.sos-notes:
> [!tip] Observations:
> - Query SoS + softplus prefactor performed best.
> - Sigmoid and Softplus baselines performed poorly.

runs-splines.page: Knots were chosen based on calibration data.

diagnostics-continued-pretraining.cpt: Each model trains for 2,000 more updates from a 1× checkpoint, fixed Taylor's or exp's, with the parameters it adds at learning rate $10^{-3}$; or from its own, keeping its coefficient optimizer state, at $10^{-4}$. Fixed Taylor's own start is its Taylor start.
diagnostics-continued-pretraining.page:
> [!info] Models
> - Query temperature: QK RMSNorm's per-head query scale $\exp(\gamma_h)$ becomes $\exp(\gamma_h + a_h \cos(w_h, x_t))$, a bounded temperature for each token and head read from the attention input $x_t$; $W$ decay is weight decay on $w_h$.

diagnostics-input-dependence.calibration-means-notes:
> [!tip] Observations:
> - Removing input dependence clearly degraded performance.
diagnostics-input-dependence.page:
> [!note] Calibration-mean intervention
> - Compute each head's average coefficients over a calibration set (64 validation sequences).
> - Fix every head's polynomial, in all layers at once, to these coefficients.
> - Evaluate the model on 256 other validation sequences.

diagnostics-length-extrapolation.ablations-notes:
> [!tip] Notes
> - Attending only to the last 2k tokens greatly improves performance.
> - Clamping RoPE at distance 2k keeps PPL stable from lengths 2k–4k, but then blows up past that.
diagnostics-length-extrapolation.position-weights-notes:
> [!tip] Notes
> - The 4k run places less weight on far away tokens, unlike the 2k run.

diagnostics-overfitting.fits: Each fit freezes a pretrained degree-4 model and trains only its coefficients on one batch of $B$ sequences: free coefficients for every sequence and query (on the fixed-Taylor model), the model's own coefficient generators, or its static coefficients. Perplexity is on that batch.
diagnostics-overfitting.regression: Coefficient generators regressed onto a free fit's coefficients (the teacher) on the frozen Taylor model. MSE runs from the Taylor start to the selected snapshot; perplexity is on the fitted batch and on 256 held-out sequences.
